Evidence · Standards

Standards work

We review draft specifications, propose language and take part in public discussion of metering boundaries, so that the acceptance criteria we use stay aligned with industry standards.

Where we take part

Open Compute Project, Cooling Environments. We follow the liquid-cooling workstream's public drafts and comment on them through the project's review process, with a focus on commissioning evidence, coolant quality and the boundaries between rack, CDU and facility. The interfaces are being specified: in 2026 Google contributed its Project Deschutes CDU specification to OCP, the first CDU specification submitted to the project, and quick-disconnect suppliers have asked for the 2019 cold-plate requirements to be updated. What a turnover package must contain is still not written down anywhere, and that is where we offer language. We are participants and reviewers, not chairs or editors of any document.

Energy-reuse metrics. The metrics that make heat reuse auditable already exist: the Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) as defined in ISO/IEC 30134-6 and EN 50600-4-6, the Energy Reuse Effectiveness (ERE) published by The Green Grid as a companion to PUE, and the metering-boundary requirement in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 for larger EU data centres. We use them in our own reporting and we argue for them in every forum where PUE is still the only number on the slide.

Public writing. The three-clock model, the ten leak points and the metering-boundary argument were all published first as open articles and posts, and revised in public with input from operators, water-chemistry specialists and insurers. The versions on this site are current and are revised as the industry discussion moves.

What we ask of the documents we review

  • Every performance requirement names the load level, temperature and boundary it applies at.
  • Every pressure boundary has a test, an acceptance criterion and a record owner.
  • Cleanliness and passivation are treated as separate requirements with separate evidence.
  • Heat reuse is measured at the hand-off boundary, not estimated from the IT load.

Questions this page answers

Which standards apply to liquid-cooling heat reuse and metering?

The Energy Reuse Factor (ERF) in ISO/IEC 30134-6 and EN 50600-4-6, the Energy Reuse Effectiveness (ERE) from The Green Grid, and the metering-boundary requirement in Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1364 for EU data centres with at least 500 kW installed IT demand. For the thermal environment itself, ASHRAE's W-classes give the facility-water temperature envelopes. Return-water grade →

Is there an open specification for liquid-cooling commissioning evidence?

Not yet. The Open Compute Project's Cooling Environments workstream publishes drafts on rack, CDU and facility interfaces, and in 2026 received its first CDU specification (Google's Project Deschutes), but none of them says what a turnover package must contain. The record structure this site uses, three questions for each of ten leak points, fills that gap. The turnover package →

Prefabricated liquid cooling for AI data centres: we plan and design the system, deliver skids, CDUs, ORv3 racks and cooling plant, and test, commission and maintain the liquid loop in the field. Every boundary comes with its evidence.
